key_insight: Scalar dissipation in passive-scalar turbulence reaches a universal anomalous limit at high Reynolds and Schmidt numbers, with scalar-gradient intermittency governed by a joint velocity-scalar multifractal cascade.
engineering_relevance: This helps predict mixing and scalar-gradient extremes in high-Schmidt flows relevant to combustion, contaminant transport, and microscale heat/mass transfer.
method: Joint multifractal model for velocity and scalar increments
Constraint by Yaglom’s law plus fluctuating Batchelor cutoff
DNS-based scaling analysis of scalar dissipation and gradient statistics
evidence_signal: Well-resolved DNS up to 8192^3, Reλ=140–1000, and Sc=1–512 show collapse of normalized dissipation and standardized scalar-gradient PDFs, supporting the predicted asymptotic and Sc-independent gradient moments.
watch_item: The asymptotic scaling requires very high Reλ at large Sc, so finite-resolution simulations or experiments may under-resolve the Batchelor scale and delay convergence.
paper_title: Scalar dissipation anomaly and scalar-gradient scaling in turbulence: A joint velocity-scalar multifractal view
